title: Worked Solution
text: To check whether events $$A$$ and $$B$$ are independent, compare the given joint probability $$P(A \text{ AND } B)$$ against the product of their individual probabilities $$P(A) \cdot P(B)$$. Because $$0.5 \cdot 0.5 = 0.25$$ does not equal the observed $$P(A \text{ AND } B) = 0.1$$, knowing one event occurred changes the likelihood of the other, so the answer is No.
